steps.text: Ductility means a material can be stretched into thin wires. Let's see which materials are ductile.
Pick a metal first — tap Copper.
Now tap “Draw Wire” and try to stretch it.
The metal stretches into a long thin wire — metals like copper, gold and aluminium are ductile. That's why wires are made of metal.
Now try a non-metal like Sulfur and draw it — it snaps instead of stretching. Metals are ductile, non-metals are not.

coach.mission: Try to draw a metal and a non-metal into a wire.
whenStuck: Tap a material first, then tap “Draw Wire”.
Try a metal like Copper, then a non-metal, and compare.
whenWrong: Metals stretch into wires (ductile); non-metals snap.
If it broke instead of stretching, that was a non-metal.
whenCorrect: Right — the metal drew into a long wire, so it's ductile.
Good — the non-metal snapped because it isn't ductile.
coach.done: You've seen that metals are ductile and non-metals are not. Try more materials, or move on when you're ready.
